reason: The registry of pure folds is kept: one driver, typed handles, snapshots at one seq, a change event per committed event. Reference identity as the change test and single-thread consistency are replaced by an explicit changed result and folding under the session append lock.

The separate JSON checkpoint store with timers and identity matching is folded into the projection registry: checkpoint rows live in the session database and commit in the transaction of the events they cover.
The whole-log statistics fold is kept as the stats view, with steps split by outcome and every settled attempt timed from the hot part of its event; it is local state and is never exported.
The turn outline is kept as the turnIndex row projection: one derived row per turn with typed previews, so a change updates one entry instead of pushing the whole outline.
Log-backed latest-wins titles, the deterministic fallback, rename and refresh are kept; Unpin is added and the single-provider registry becomes a registry seam with one active provider chosen by id.

The shared execution policy becomes the generator inside the title component: it logs and flushes the request event, builds the request from that event, sends it, and settles it with exactly one attempt event under one acceptance rule.
The first-prompt strategy becomes a title.Provider (prompt framing and cadence only) registered by the title-llm component; scheduling and the model call belong to the generator.

The capture coordinator, live capture mode, operational records and in-memory hand-off cursor are replaced by a session-upload component whose consent and delivery progress are session events; redaction is an ordered registry with a built-in baseline.

Upload after explicit own feedback is kept as a rule, but it is off by default, needs a confirmed preview per submission, and sends through the harness's own OTLP channel owned by area A18 instead of the OpenTelemetry SDK.
One logged directory per session with Get, Ensure and Set, recovery to the original project, an access coordination key and a required context entry is kept; only host operations move it.

A quote stays ordinary Markdown: Go functions encode selected text as blockquote lines and recognise them at render time; the selection action and display belong to the composer and conversation UI areas (C3, C4).
The query service is kept as the Query interface: listing, one-cut observation, bounded event windows, traces and lineage, now with a required visibility and no method that returns a whole log.

The separate derived search database with per-search reconciliation is folded into the store-backed query component: search documents are a row projection committed with their events in the session database.
The two read-only listing tools are kept as a separate query-tools component, with keyset cursors, a blank filter, a title state and visibility limited to the caller's workspace by default.

The ZIP archive and Markdown transcript are kept as functions that write to any writer, with a manifest and a final status; the routes, the command and the UI controls belong to areas A19, A24 and the UI areas.
The untyped keyed read kept for old plugins has no Go counterpart: state is read only through the typed handle returned by Register.
A read that returns only cells some other read happened to compute does not exist: a snapshot returns every requested key with an explicit state of current, behind or pending.
The writerless working-directory/change event is not registered in the Go event vocabulary, so there is nothing for readers to ignore.
The archive and transcript functions write to any io.Writer, so a command (dsh session export --out) writes a host file atomically as well as the browser download.
An HTTP export is a host-tracked operation whose final status (complete, complete with omissions, failed) reaches the tab's event stream, and the archive ends with a manifest of omissions.
Half of the limit is removed and half is kept: the transcript now states the cut it was taken at, marks an open turn and offers log scope or surface scope, but unsettled stream text is still absent.
justification: Kept on purpose: a view reads committed events only (design.md section 4.6), so text that has not settled into an event cannot be in a transcript. DH-D-VIEW-8 builds the explicit cut and the open-turn mark that replace the silent omission. The stage is a placeholder because the implementation plan is not written.

reason: The transcript formatter takes an option to include descendant sessions as sections, bounded by the caller's visibility.
The host streams the transcript without holding it whole; above a configured size the UI offers a file download instead of a clipboard copy and never truncates.
The limit describes a client plugin being disposed while a clipboard write is in flight; the Go design has no client plugin runtime, only a host-rendered page with one copy gesture (DH-ADR-3).
There is no per-session file whose path could lag the live log: the session id, the cut and the events of a transcript come from one read transaction of the session database.
Every Query method, search included, requires a Visibility whose zero value sees nothing, so access is enforced in the service and not left to each tool.
A search runs on its own goroutine with a cancellable context that stops the statement within the driver's bound, so nothing blocks the host.

Substring recall no longer needs a second, per-session call: one search request has a literal mode that scans the stored text of the whole corpus, and Chinese, Japanese and Korean text is prepared as overlapping two-character pieces so substrings match in ranked mode too. A token index still ranks by tokens for space-separated scripts. Provisional on measurement M3.
Index rows are written in the event's own transaction by whichever process holds the session lease, so several processes share one index in the one database.
Visibility is a required argument of every Query method and a hidden session is reported as not found, so the service itself constrains what a caller may inspect.
Search is not a separate backend to mount: it is part of the store-backed query component, and with indexing configured off it reports query/search-disabled while exact reads keep working.
Reads are ranges by seq against the store, and surface class and citation links are derived rows written with the events, so no read replays a whole log.
One search request offers a ranked mode and a literal mode over the same stored documents and the same filters, for one session or the whole corpus.
List values commit with their events, and each item carries a title_state of current, behind or pending, so a null title means only that the session has no title.

Listing is a keyset page on an index, ordered as of the first call, so work is bounded by the page size and entries do not move between calls. A session deleted or archived meanwhile is no longer returned, which is intended.
A blank flag is a list column and list_session takes include_blank, which defaults to false.
The tool test drives both the scoped and the unscoped listing through the executor in keyless replay, so neither form has unit coverage only.
Tool visibility is derived from the initiating agent and a configured policy that defaults to the caller's own workspace; mounting the tools no longer grants the whole runtime.
Half of the limit is removed and half is kept: lines inside a fenced code block are no longer recognised as quotes, but Markdown lazy continuation is still not implemented.
justification: Kept on purpose: with lazy continuation, text the user types on the line after a quote would be shown as part of the quote, so only explicitly marked lines are quotes, as upstream decided. DH-D-VIEW-8 builds the recogniser with the fenced-code rule. The stage is a placeholder because the implementation plan is not written.

reason: Checkpoint rows are deleted in the store's delete-session transaction and a prune removes rows whose key no binary registers.
There is no interval timer: checkpoints are tied to commits (every commit for list state; turn end, close and every N events for the rest).
The registry reads the store itself and folds the missing suffix inside one read transaction, so no consumer has to refold from the log.

Stored state is disposable: a version mismatch discards and refolds, so there is no record format to prove upgrades for, and one property test (checkpoint plus suffix equals full fold) replaces archived fixtures.
Every read names the keys it wants and the host renders only those; a value that grows with the session (the turn index) is stored as rows and read in pages.
The table of registered folds stays host-wide in the Go design, so a registered key exists for every session and its presence still says nothing about one session's capabilities.
justification: Kept on purpose: a fold is a function of the log and must be defined for every session, including sessions no agent holds, or listing would depend on which agents are live. The hazard is removed by DH-D-VIEW-1: the host renders pages, an unknown key is an error, and whether a feature is on is asked of the composition, so no reader infers anything from key presence. The stage is a placeholder because the implementation plan is not written.

reason: A definition declares the event types it consumes and the registry dispatches by type, so an event visits only the folds that asked for it.
A stored row carries the seq it covers, so a reader sees it as behind and never as current, and the next registration of the key catches up from it.

The retained definition exists because upstream hot-reloads plugin modules and lets readers outlive their owner; Go loads no code at run time and the cordis port unloads dependents first, so nothing keeps a released definition.
Fold state is checkpointed in the session database in the transaction of the events it covers, so a restart reads rows instead of refolding.
Fold functions live in leaf packages whose imports are checked (no I/O, clocks or randomness), every definition runs the equivalence and determinism tests, and a slow fold is measured and reported.
The stats view reports closed steps and steps with visible output as separate figures, so attempted work and shown work are both readable.
Every settled attempt, including a cancelled or failed one, carries its times in the hot part of its event, so all attempts are timed and model time is one figure that says what it covers.
Both scopes are offered and labelled: the fold counts the whole log, and Query counts events whose class is current from derived rows.
The projection registry is a spine service and the browser never folds events, so there is no client fallback to diverge; a composition without the stats entry simply renders no strip.
No OpenTelemetry SDK is linked; the OTLP exporter is harness code on the standard library, owned by area A18.
Collector-facing behaviour (deadlines, retry, limits) is specified and tested in the harness's own exporter instead of being inherited from an SDK.

Authorisation and delivered-through are session events, so an upload has a watermark, advances only on the collector's acknowledgement, resumes after a restart and is delivered at least once. That a sent record cannot be recalled is outside any client's power; the confirmation tells the user before sending.
With upload off no consent is asked, so there is nothing to replay; a confirmed upload is a logged fact found by a fold, not a live notification that an unloaded component can miss.
The hand-off cursor in memory is replaced by logged authorisation and delivery events: the uploader reads events after the watermark, so a crash or reload loses no authorised record.
A baseline redactor always runs last and cannot be removed or skipped: it masks secret values the credential store released and recognised secret shapes. It is pattern-based and the preview says so.
The consent event records the fingerprint of the rule set the preview was computed with; an upload under a different rule set sends nothing and asks for a new confirmation.
With the default first-prompt cadence a title is still generated once, from the first message, and can stop describing a long session.
justification: Kept on purpose for the default: one auxiliary model call per session is the cost the default accepts. The remedies are built by DH-D-VIEW-4: Refresh summarises all eligible prompts and is a user action in the UI, the command line and the SDK, and another provider cadence can be selected by id. The stage is a placeholder because the implementation plan is not written.

reason: A fork generates a title on its first own prompt unless its inherited title is pinned by the user, so two list rows do not share one title.
One acceptance rule lives in the generator (finish stop, a non-empty first line, within the byte limit after cleaning); providers supply the prompt only.
Input over the ceiling is reduced at message boundaries (first prompt plus the newest that fit, one message clipped at a character boundary), and the request event records exactly what was sent.
Reasoning effort is one configuration field of the generator with the default lowest, not a function each provider implements.
Unpin returns a session to automatic titles, title events are search documents, and the title is a plain list column that can be filtered.
Providers register by id in a registry seam and configuration selects the one that is active, so precedence is a setting and not code in a combined provider.
The turn index is derived rows, one per turn, so a change writes and pushes one entry and the page reads a window.
An open turn's row carries the latest committed assistant text marked unsettled, which is cheap once an update touches one row.
Each entry carries a kind (text, images, files, command, tools only) and a count, so the page shows a localised label instead of a bare turn number.
The registry is a spine service and no client folds events, so there is no loaded-window fallback to diverge; a composition without the entry renders no outline.
No Go log can hold a directory the model moved, because that event type is never registered; what an imported upstream log maps to is the importer's decision (DH-ADR-11).
When the current directory and the original project are both gone, the Go design still rejects every model turn and still does not choose or recreate a directory.
justification: Kept on purpose by DH-ADR-VIEW-8: the write boundary is resolved from the directory, so guessing one would not fail closed. What is removed is the dead end: DH-D-VIEW-10 returns the typed error workdir/unavailable, on which the UI, the command line and the SDK offer the choice of an existing directory. The stage is a placeholder because the implementation plan is not written.

reason: The Go harness exposes list_session, changed: a keyset cursor replaces offset, include_blank is added, the result is an object with items, next_cursor and as_of, each item carries a title_state, and only sessions the caller's visibility admits are returned.

The Go harness exposes list_workspace, changed: a keyset cursor replaces offset and the result is an object with items and next_cursor, read from the workspace registry of area A07 under the caller's visibility.

The redaction waterfall is replaced by upload.Redactors, an ordered registry of functions that may change or withhold a record; unlike a waterfall listener, a redactor cannot skip the others, and the built-in baseline always runs last.

The Go typed event workdir.Access replaces it in the around form: a listener may wait for an operation on the directory and then proceeds or denies with a reason; a denial leaves the recorded directory unchanged.
transcript.Config replaces it: CompressionLevel 0 to 9 with default 6, plus MaxCopyBytes for the clipboard cap.
projection.Config replaces it: CheckpointEveryEvents stays (default 200), the interval field is gone with the timer, and catch-up and rebuild bounds are added.

query.Config replaces it: page, snippet and window limits are kept with the same defaults; path, openAt, journalMode and the cold-read cache fields have no counterpart because the index is in the store that area A05 opens.
upload.Config replaces it: mode becomes Enabled with default false, the endpoint and headers are explicit, the byte ceiling is kept, and queue settings belong to area A18's channel.
title.Config replaces it with the same three limits; the defaults are the values upstream's base bundle sets (5 words, 40 bytes, 80 bytes), and the active provider id is added.
title.GeneratorConfig replaces it with the same targets, input and output caps, timeout and optional route, defaulted to the base bundle's values, plus reasoning effort and the fork rule.
workdir.Config replaces it with the one field DefaultDirectory, which must be absolute and defaults to the launch directory.
There is no separate cache service: checkpoint reads and writes are part of the projection registry behind projection.Key.
The service key projection.Key with the Registry interface (Snapshot, Rebuild, Status) and the generic Register function replace ctx.sessionProjections.
The service key query.Key with the Query interface replaces ctx.sessionQuery; every method takes a Visibility and search is concrete.

The service key upload.Key with the Uploads interface (Status, Preview, Authorise, Cancel) replaces ctx.sessionTelemetry; there is no emit method, so no caller can send a record outside a confirmed upload.
The service key title.Key with the Titles interface (Get, Rename, Unpin, Refresh) and the title.Providers registry replace ctx.sessionTitle.
The service key workdir.Key with the Service interface (Get, Ensure, Set) replaces ctx.workingDirectory.

Kept: a reader of projected state requires the registry, a missing registry or key is an error and never a default, and one change event is raised per committed event. Go adds an explicit behind and pending state so that 'not ready' is also never a default.

The rule is kept: every exact read is one observation with one cut, and values shown to clients come only from registered folds. The mechanism changes: a read transaction replaces the prepared-session cache and its leases, and a read may name keys.

The consent rule is kept (only a new, own, explicit feedback submission authorises an upload; inherited feedback does not) and tightened by the owner's decision: off by default, a preview confirmed per submission, and one off-switch.

Kept: one service owns one logged directory per session, the header keeps the original project as identity and recovery destination, and the directory reaches the model as user context and never through the system prompt.

The projection half is adopted: state-carrying events hold whole values and registered pure folds are driven by one registry, which suits a server-rendered page where the latest fragment replaces the previous one. The command-log half belongs to the commands area (A17).

Both rules of the note repair a cache that is a different store with its own sequence space. A checkpoint row keyed by session in the session's own database needs no identity witness or fork cut, and every seq it carries is the log's, so there is no cached-versus-sequenced distinction to keep.

Typed handles returned by registration are kept. Readers that survive unregistration and the callable-promise compatibility shim are not: the Go cordis port unloads dependents before their provider, and registration needs no asynchronous step.
Kept as a field: a definition says whether list rows carry it (Summary), and list reads take only those keys. The type-level exclusion mark is a TypeScript device with no Go counterpart.

Kept: only host operations move the directory, no model tool does, there is one read, and each move is a workspace-root/change event. The sandbox resolver reads that directory as the workspace root, which is why a model-chosen move is not allowed.

Kept: a quote is ordinary Markdown recognised when a message is rendered, with no stored quote index. The host renderer calls the recogniser; fenced code is excluded and lazy continuation stays out on purpose.

Adopted: the Go Query interface offers observations, batch titles, surface pages, event windows, traces, lineage, listing and search, and has no method that returns a whole log or a single-title convenience read.

title: A projection is a typed pure fold with declared inputs, driven by one registry
Stored state commits with its events; a reader is told current, behind or pending
Indexes are projections: list columns, turn index, event classes and search documents
Every query takes a visibility and is bounded; no method returns a whole log
Search prepares CJK text in Go over stock FTS5, with a ranked and a literal mode
A title call is logged before it is sent, attributed, and settled by exactly one event
Session upload is opt-in, confirmed per submission, logged, redacted and resumable
One working directory per session; a person moves it anywhere, a tool call only inside the anchor
Exports write to any writer and end with a status
Folds are registered once and read at one cut
Stored state is never ahead of the log, and a changed fold rebuilds itself
The built-in views: list summary, turn index, statistics, event index
Sessions have titles, and the model call that writes one is in the log
Sessions can be listed, observed, traced and followed across forks, within what the caller may see
Full-text search finds text in any script, in every process, as soon as it is committed
The model can list workspaces and sessions, bounded and scoped
A session can be taken away as an archive or a transcript, and quotes are plain text
A session is uploaded only after the user confirmed exactly what is sent
Every tool of a session works in the same directory, and only the host moves it
A checkpoint at any cut plus the suffix equals a full fold, for every registered definition
Under concurrent appends every snapshot equals a refold through its AsOfSeq
Registration rules: required registry, one version per key, unknown key is an error, dispatch by declared type
Fold packages pass the import check and fold deterministically; a slow fold is reported
Fault injection in a commit: stored state is never ahead of stored events and a failing derived write loses no event
A version bump discards stored state; a rebuild resumes after a kill and equals a fresh fold
Reader states: Stored never blocks, Exact catches up or fails with view/behind, a panicking fold fails one key
A fork's state equals a fold of its logical log; delete and prune remove the right derived rows
Golden logs for the list summary, turn index, statistics and event index folds
Title cleaning, safe truncation, fallback limits, pin and unpin
The title request sent equals the one rebuilt from the log, is flushed first, and settles exactly once
Title scheduling: once per fresh session, forks, subagents, stale results, input reduction, no route fallback, no turn delay
Bounded windows, surface classes, traces and lineage across forks
Visibility: the zero value sees nothing and a hidden session looks missing in every method
Keyset listing returns each visible session once under concurrent change, with work bounded by the page
Search corpus in English, Chinese, Japanese and Korean: hits, literal operators, stable order, rebuilt equals incremental
Benchmark M3: append cost and index size per tokenisation option (a recorded result)
List tools through the executor and in keyless replay: schema, limits, cursor, scoped and unscoped, result bound
Golden archive and transcript: manifest with omissions, safe names, both scopes, bounded memory, atomic file
Quote recognition: explicit lines, fenced code excluded, no lazy continuation, round trip
Upload consent: nothing is sent by default, without confirmation, from inherited consent, after the off-switch or under a changed rule set
Upload delivery and redaction: watermark on acknowledgement, resume after restart, masking, preview equals what is sent
Working directory rules: Get, Set, SetForCall inside the anchor only, recovery through the access key, both missing, denial, unchanged header
No default tool moves the directory; a mounted worktree tool moves it only inside the anchor; its context is logged and the next call uses it
Budgets for list, ranked search and a large snapshot; the tree message timeline and the single-session literal search are bounded and visibility-checked
A real model titles a session, and a failing provider leaves the fallback
After the host is killed mid-turn, every view equals a refold of the log
A second process lists and searches a session another process is writing
Nothing is uploaded without consent, and a confirmed upload survives a restart
A host move into a real worktree changes where tools work and what they may write
In a real browser: search in two scripts, an export with a final status, a transcript copy
